/// Returns the checked Integer. Call checkInteger again to check it against different bounds.
public function value(value: CheckedInteger) -> Integer
  return CheckedInteger.value(value)
end function

implement Trait.Show[RangeError]
  function show(x: RangeError) -> String
    return match x with
      case RangeError.InvalidBounds(minimum, maximum) -> "InvalidBounds(${minimum}, ${maximum})"
      case RangeError.OutOfRange(minimum, maximum, value) -> "OutOfRange(${minimum}, ${maximum}, ${value})"
    end match
  end function
end implement

/// A list and its checked inclusive length bounds. This wrapper retains the original list, including references in its elements.
@opaque
public record CheckedLength[T]
  minimum: Integer
  maximum: Integer
  length: Integer
  values: List[T]
end record

/// InvalidBounds takes priority over OutOfRange. Failures retain only bounds and the actual length, never the list.
public data LengthError
  InvalidBounds(Integer, Integer)
  OutOfRange(Integer, Integer, Integer)
end data

/// Checks the element count. A negative minimum or reversed bounds is rejected before comparing the length. Constant invalid inputs still return Result.Error.
public function checkLength[T](minimum: Integer, maximum: Integer, values: List[T]) -> Result[CheckedLength[T], LengthError]
  if minimum < 0 or maximum < minimum then
    return Result.Error(LengthError.InvalidBounds(minimum, maximum))
  end if
  bind length <- List.length(values)
  return if length < minimum or maximum < length then Result.Error(LengthError.OutOfRange(minimum, maximum, length))
  else Result.Ok(CheckedLength(minimum: minimum, maximum: maximum, length: length, values: values)) end if
end function

/// Returns the inclusive minimum length retained by the check.
public function lengthMinimum[T](value: CheckedLength[T]) -> Integer
  return CheckedLength.minimum(value)

end function

/// A list, its checked zero-based index and the element found there. This wrapper retains the original list.
@opaque
public record CheckedIndex[T]
  values: List[T]
  index: Integer
  element: T
end record

/// The rejected index and the element count. The original list is not retained.
public data IndexError
  OutOfBounds(Integer, Integer)
end data

/// Checks the zero-based index and retains its successful element. Both negative and too-large indices return OutOfBounds, including constant inputs.
public function checkIndex[T](index: Integer, values: List[T]) -> Result[CheckedIndex[T], IndexError]
  return match List.get(xs: values, i: index) with
    case Option.None -> Result.Error(IndexError.OutOfBounds(index, List.length(values)))
    case Option.Some(element) -> Result.Ok(CheckedIndex(values: values, index: index, element: element))
  end match
end function

/// Returns the zero-based index retained by the check.
public function indexValue[T](value: CheckedIndex[T]) -> Integer
  return CheckedIndex.index(value)
end function

/// Returns the original immutable list retained by the check.
public function indexValues[T](value: CheckedIndex[T]) -> List[T]
  return CheckedIndex.values(value)
end function

/// Returns the element found during construction. A different list requires a new checkIndex call.
public function get[T](value: CheckedIndex[T]) -> T
  return CheckedIndex.element(value)
end function

implement Trait.Show[LengthError]
  function show(x: LengthError) -> String
    return match x with
      case LengthError.InvalidBounds(minimum, maximum) -> "InvalidBounds(${minimum}, ${maximum})"
      case LengthError.OutOfRange(minimum, maximum, length) -> "OutOfRange(${minimum}, ${maximum}, ${length})"
    end match
  end function
end implement

implement Trait.Show[IndexError]
  function show(x: IndexError) -> String
    return match x with
      case IndexError.OutOfBounds(index, length) -> "OutOfBounds(${index}, ${length})"
    end match
  end function
end implement

public record NonEmptyList[T]
  first: T
  rest: List[T]
end record

/// Construction failed because the input list was empty. The input list is not retained.
public data EmptyListError
  EmptyList
end data

/// Checks whether the list is nonempty. Even a constant empty input returns Result.Error.
public function fromList[T](values: List[T]) -> Result[NonEmptyList[T], EmptyListError]
  return match values with
    case [] -> Result.Error(EmptyListError.EmptyList)
    case [head, ..tail] -> Result.Ok(NonEmptyList(first: head, rest: tail))
  end match
end function

/// Returns all elements in the original order, preserving shared Reference elements.
public function toList[T](value: NonEmptyList[T]) -> List[T]
  return List.prepend(xs: NonEmptyList.rest(value), x: NonEmptyList.first(value))
end function

/// Returns the first element, without a second check or an Option wrapper.
public function head[T](value: NonEmptyList[T]) -> T
  return NonEmptyList.first(value)
end function

/// Returns the remaining elements, which may be empty.
public function tail[T](value: NonEmptyList[T]) -> List[T]
  return NonEmptyList.rest(value)
end function

/// Applies f once to each element, from first to last. Effects and failures propagate; a successful result remains nonempty.
public function map[T, U, effect E](value: NonEmptyList[T], f: function(value: T) -> U uses E) -> NonEmptyList[U] uses E
  bind head <- f(NonEmptyList.first(value))
  bind tail <- List.map(xs: NonEmptyList.rest(value), f: f)
  return NonEmptyList(first: head, rest: tail)
end function

implement Trait.Show[EmptyListError]
  function show(x: EmptyListError) -> String
    return match x with
      case EmptyListError.EmptyList -> "EmptyList"
    end match
  end function
end implement
